office_does: A Thurston PUD commissioner sits on the three-member board of a water utility that runs 271 water systems serving about 25,000 people, adopting its budget and setting rates, for a six-year term.
race_blurb: Commissioner Chris Stearns is not on the ballot, leaving an open seat. State drinking-water loan program manager Chris Pettit, endorsed by all three sitting commissioners, faces small business owner Jeff Curry, a Scott Lake water-district board member running on affordability and solar.

candidates.summary: Small business owner and Scott Lake community water-district board member making his fifth run for office since 2022, on affordability, solar power and a water-quality app.
highlights: Utility experience is a board seat for the Scott Lake community water district [S1]
Pledges to keep rates reasonable and be transparent about utility spending [S1]
Proposes adding solar to the local grid and a public water-quality mobile app [S1]
Ran for county treasurer (2022), Tumwater school board (2023, 2025) and governor (2024) without winning [S4]

candidates.summary: Attorney and state Drinking Water State Revolving Fund program manager, former Washington Conservation Commission director, running for his first elected office on affordability, transparency and conservation.
highlights: Manages the state Drinking Water State Revolving Fund, which lends to the PUD; previously led the Washington State Conservation Commission [S1][S6]
Cites a 25% rise in rates over five years and would pursue cost reductions from a legislative utility-affordability report [S1][S7]
Would expand advisory groups and make rate and budget documents easier to understand [S7]
Endorsed by all three sitting PUD commissioners and by county and city officials [S2]
